comment: Evidence nodes are referenced by edge.evidence_ids. P1 stores them so every path step can be traced to a source; the SUPPORTED_BY edges land in P2 with Findings.

props.excerpt:
on:
  pull_request_target:
permissions: write-all
jobs:
  build:
    steps:
      - uses: ./.github/actions/deploy
        env:
          DEPLOY_KEY: ${{ secrets.PROD_DEPLOY_KEY }}
props.supports_claim: build.yml runs with write-all permissions on pull_request_target and consumes PROD_DEPLOY_KEY.
props.limitations: Static read of the file at one commit. Does not prove the job executed.

props.excerpt:
agents:
  - name: code-assistant
    mcp_servers: [filesystem-mcp, github-mcp]
filesystem-mcp:
  tools: [read_file, write_file]
  permissions:
    read:  src/**
    write: '**'
props.supports_claim: code-assistant may invoke write_file, whose write permission is scoped to the entire repository.
props.limitations: Declared configuration. Effective permission at runtime is not verified here.

props.supports_claim: The write scope ** includes .github/workflows/**, so the permission reaches the workflow file class.
props.limitations: Evaluates the declared glob only. Does not account for branch protection or CODEOWNERS.

props.supports_claim: code-assistant actually invokes write_file, so CAN_INVOKE is observed and not merely declared.
props.limitations: One observed call against src/**. No observed write to .github/**.

props.supports_claim: node-fetch 2.6.1 falls inside the advisory's affected range.
props.limitations: Manifest-level match. Reachability of the vulnerable code path is untested.
